newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Savimbi wants high-level invite to talks - UNITA.
newsitem.headline: Savimbi wants high-level invite to talks - UNITA.

text.p: Angola's opposition UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi would attend a regional summit in Luanda on Wednesday only if he is invited by President Jonas Eduardo dos Santos himself, a senior UNITA official said on Monday.

Abel Chivukuvuku, the party's chief constitutional negotiator, told reporters Savimbi had been invited to the peace talks by Zambian President Frederick Chiluba but UNITA felt this was not appropriate.
"It would be legitimate if the president of Zambia invited Dr Savimbi to go to Lusaka, but to come to Luanda we think it should be the president of the country (dos Santos) who invites him.
"It is not logical that a foreign head of state invites an Angolan citizen to come to the capital," Chivukuvuku said.

South African President Nelson Mandela is among leaders of the 12-member Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) due to attend the talks aimed at speeding up implementation of Angola's peace process.
UNITA and the dos Santos government signed an accord in November 1994 to end their 19-year civil war.
SADC links Angola, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, Malawi, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Mauritius, Lesotho and Swaziland.
